_meta.indication: Treatment of adults with cervical dystonia (to decrease severity of abnormal head position and neck pain in both botulinum toxin-naive and previously treated patients) and treatment of adults with blepharospasm who were previously treated with onabotulinumtoxinA (Botox)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Phase 3 placebo-controlled cervical dystonia trial (120 U and 240 U vs placebo)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-center trial with XEOMIN initial doses of 120 Units and 240 Units versus placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with predominantly rotational cervical dystonia (baseline TWSTRS total score ≥ 20); 61% previously received a botulinum toxin for cervical dystonia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in TWSTRS total score from baseline to Week 4 post-injection in the ITT population
pivotal_trials.result: TWSTRS total score difference vs placebo at Week 4: 240 U group -9.0 points (95% CI -12.0; -5.9); 120 U group -7.5 points (95% CI -10.4; -4.6); each XEOMIN group vs placebo p<0.001

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Confirmatory trial of NT 201 for blepharospasm (MRZ 60201-0433/1)
pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized, multi-center trial (34 centers in US and Canada) with patients randomized 2:1 to XEOMIN or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with benign essential blepharospasm (baseline JRS Severity subscore ≥ 2) with a stable satisfactory therapeutic response to previous onabotulinumtoxinA (Botox)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in JRS Severity subscore from baseline to Week 6 post-injection in the ITT population
pivotal_trials.result: JRS Severity subscore difference between XEOMIN and placebo at Week 6 was -1.0 (95% CI -1.4; -0.5) points; XEOMIN vs placebo statistically significant at p<0.001

key_safety: Cervical dystonia most common adverse reactions: dysphagia (120U 13%, 240U 18% vs placebo 3%), neck pain, muscle weakness, injection site pain, musculoskeletal pain. Blepharospasm most common: eyelid ptosis, dry eye, dry mouth, diarrhea, headache, visual impairment, dyspnea, nasopharyngitis, respiratory tract infection.
target_moa: Botulinum neurotoxin type A that blocks cholinergic transmission at the neuromuscular junction by inhibiting release of acetylcholine from peripheral cholinergic nerve endings (acetylcholine release inhibitor / neuromuscular blocking agent)
modality: other (botulinum neurotoxin type A biologic protein)

boxed_warning.content: Distant Spread of Toxin Effect: effects may spread from the injection area to produce botulinum toxin effects; swallowing and breathing difficulties can be life threatening and there have been reports of death

rems.type: REMS required to ensure benefits outweigh risk of distant spread of toxin and potential medication errors from lack of interchangeability; consists of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for assessments

advisory_committee.vote: Application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this biologic is not the first in its class and the safety profile is similar to other approved drugs for these indications

citations.quote: Please refer to Biologics License Application (BLA) dated July 1, 2009, received July 2, 2009, submitted by Merz Pharmaceuticals under section 351 of the Public Health Service Act for Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxinA) Injection.

Your application for Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxinA) was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this biologic is not the first in its class, and the safety profile is similar to that of other drugs approved for these indications.

In accordance with 505-1 of the FDA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxinA) to ensure that the benefits of the drug outweigh the risk of distant spread of botulinum toxin after local injection, and the potential for medication errors related to the lack of interchangeability of Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxinA) with other licensed botulinum toxin products.
